From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: PHI dataflow boundaries & BAA routing — post-call action items

Hi Anika / Tom — great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so MediCourt can complete your internal risk review. Note: copying Aditya (sales lead) and Marissa (security engagement) so they have context.

Summary of what we covered (high level)
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report for our control plane and operational processes; the most recent report is in our secure drive (link below). We are currently in a renewal window but controls and evidence remain consistent with the prior report.
- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments immediately. For Hosted API (shared tenancy) we require a short legal/security intake and a minimum enterprise commitment before executing a hosted BAA — we discussed your expected usage and this is typically handled during procurement.
- PHI handling boundaries: Primary options we outlined for PHI workloads:
  * Private (customer-managed control plane or on-prem): full control over data persistence, logging, and KMS. Best when MediCourt needs strict egress controls and full auditability.
  * Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): isolated hardware and tenant-level control; data persistence policies are configurable (you can require no persistence).
  * Hosted (shared): ephemeral-by-default (no persistent storage of prompts or KV cache unless explicitly enabled by customer). We provide an option for zero-persist (no chat logs, no model-cache writes), but hosted BAA is conditional as noted above.
- Embeddings & caches: embeddings are not stored by default unless customer enables a vector store managed by them or explicitly asks Redwood to host persistent embeddings. KV cache for ongoing chat sessions can be configured to be ephemeral (in-memory only) or flushed after each session.

Action items (agreed on call)
1) Soojin: attach the HIPAA requirements matrix and the BAA summary PDF (attached).
2) MediCourt: send the vendor security questionnaire (we can pre-fill common answers) and flag any EHR integration scenarios you expect.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive next week focused on dataflow and KMS integration — propose Tue/Wed morning PT.
4) Redwood: provide SOC 2 packet and a short note on logging/retention policy for hosted vs. dedicated.

Attachments: HIPAA-reqs-matrix.xlsx (mapping of PHI categories to hosting options), redwood-baa-summary.pdf (high-level BAA coverage and timelines).

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive: Tue 11/10 9:30-10:15 PT or Wed 11/11 10:00-10:45 PT. Please confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — helpful summary. A few clarifying questions before we kick off the questionnaire:

1) For hosted deployments when you say "zero-persist," can you confirm that:
   - the KV cache lives in-memory only and is flushed after session close unless we explicitly enable persistence?
   - request/response payloads are not written to disk or long-term logs by default?
2) Embeddings: if MediCourt uses Redwood-managed embeddings (for semantic search), is there an option to have those stored in our own VPC customer-managed store, or do they live in Redwood's managed store?
3) BAA scope: Will the BAA cover EHR integrations (API calls to third-party EHR vendors) if the integration is initiated from within a Redwood-hosted model runtime?

Also can you share where to retrieve the SOC 2 Type II report and the name/email of the Redwood contact who signs BAAs? Security wants to confirm the signee is an authorized legal representative.

Appreciate it — once we have these items we can complete the vendor security questionnaire and circle back on timelines.

Regards,

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PHI dataflow boundaries & BAA routing — post-call action items

Hi Anika — answers inline below to keep everything in one thread. Marissa will join the deep-dive to go deeper on encryption and logging.

On Mon, Nov 8, 2026 at 4:12 PM Anika Rao <anika@medicourt.com> wrote:
> 1) For hosted deployments when you say "zero-persist," can you confirm that:
>    - the KV cache lives in-memory only and is flushed after session close unless we explicitly enable persistence?
>    - request/response payloads are not written to disk or long-term logs by default?

Yes to both with the following nuance:
- Hosted: by default KV cache is in-memory and flushed; request/response payloads are not written to long-term logs unless you enable request logging for analytics. We provide an explicit "no-persist" toggle for sessions that ensures no logs, no disk writes, and no model-cache persistence.
- Dedicated/Private: you can opt for in-memory-only runtime and also lock configuration so no persistence is possible. For customers that want maximal assurance we recommend Private (customer-managed) where you control the storage backend and keys.

> 2) Embeddings: if MediCourt uses Redwood-managed embeddings (for semantic search), is there an option to have those stored in our own VPC customer-managed store, or do they live in Redwood's managed store?

You have both options:
- Redwood-managed vector store (default): hosted by Redwood — embedding persistence is configurable and can be disabled. If enabled, we encrypt at rest and keys are managed by Redwood KMS by default.
- Customer-managed vector store: recommended for PHI — embeddings can be written to a customer-managed store in your VPC (S3/Blob) or to an on-prem store and Raven (our ops team) will provide the integration hooks. That option is available for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted it's available but requires additional procurement/legal steps.

> 3) BAA scope: Will the BAA cover EHR integrations (API calls to third-party EHR vendors) if the integration is initiated from within a Redwood-hosted model runtime?

The BAA covers processing of PHI by Redwood services. For EHR integrations that pass PHI to third-party EHR vendors, coverage depends on dataflow ownership: if Redwood processes/transforms PHI and you require Redwood to persist or log that PHI, it falls under the BAA. If Redwood only orchestrates a call and no PHI payload is ever routed through Redwood (e.g., direct EHR API from your VPC), then Redwood's BAA may not apply. We recommend we review any specific EHR integration flows in the technical deep-dive so Legal can map responsibilities precisely.

> Also can you share where to retrieve the SOC 2 Type II report and the name/email of the Redwood contact who signs BAAs?

SOC 2: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/hipaa/SOC2-Redwood-2026-TypeII (we will provide read-only access to your security team).
BAA signee: Our authorized signatory is Claudia Mendes (Legal) — claudia.mendes@redwood.ai. For Hosted BAAs there is a standard intake form Legal requires; for Dedicated/Private we can typically sign the standard BAA within 5 business days after countersignature.

Next steps (concrete)
- I will: (a) share SOC 2 link + HIPAA reqs matrix (attached), (b) send a pre-filled version of your vendor questionnaire today so you can review and modify, (c) schedule the technical deep-dive with Marissa and our infra lead for Tue 11/10 9:30 PT as proposed.
- You: confirm if you want Redwood-managed embeddings or customer-managed store for the PoC, and share any EHR vendors / endpoints you expect to hit during the PoC.

If it's helpful, Marissa can circulate a short one-page diagram of the default hosted vs. dedicated vs. private dataflows prior to the call.

Best,
Soojin

Attachments referenced: HIPAA-reqs-matrix.xlsx, redwood-baa-summary.pdf
